Hugh Lofting, The Story of Doctor Dolittle.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/hugh-lofting/the-story-of-doctor-dolittle

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Hugh Lofting, the author, died 1947.

First publication of the text used: 1920 (SE colophon: 'The Story of Doctor Dolittle was published in 1920 by Hugh Lofting'; Wikipedia, 'The Story of Doctor Dolittle': published in the United States by Frederick A. Stokes on October 25, 1920, before its UK publication by Cape in 1924).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in the United States on 25 October 1920, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published in the United States in 1920, before 1931, so the United States rule above settles the country of origin whatever the death year.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: published in 1920 by Hugh Lofting; no other publication date given.
- Wikidata Q560015 (Hugh Lofting), P570 = 1947-09-26
- Wikipedia, The Story of Doctor Dolittle (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_of_Doctor_Dolittle): published in the United States by Frederick A. Stokes on October 25, 1920; UK publication by Cape in 1924
